Tutorial 7: Core Pipeline Functions and Methodological Dictionary

Beatriz M. Meriño

2026-10-20

Source: vignettes/tutorial-7-cactus-phylogeny-functions.Rmd
tutorial-7-cactus-phylogeny-functions.Rmd

Abstract

This page lists the main functions of the PhyloCactus workflow, grouped by stage, with the method each one implements and its primary reference. Arguments and return values are documented in the manual pages and in the pkgdown reference index.

Functions by Stage

Sequence Assembly

Function Description Reference
assemble_ingroup_phylotar() Retrieves sequence clusters for the ingroup (Cactaceae, NCBI Taxonomy ID 3593) from GenBank with phylotaR. Clusters are formed by sequence similarity, not by GenBank locus annotations; gene-name synonyms are mapped with genes_map.csv, clusters with more than min_species species are retained, and a curated list of excluded accessions is applied. Bennett et al. (2018)
assemble_outgroup_phylotar() Retrieves sequence clusters for the outgroup genera of Anacampserotaceae, Portulacaceae and Talinaceae, for the loci selected in the ingroup. Bennett et al. (2018)
fetch_genbank_metadata() Retrieves the organism name and definition line of each GenBank accession through ape::read.GenBank(), in batches with retries, and caches them. Paradis & Schliep (2019)

Alignment and Quality Control

Function Description Reference
run_alignment_pipeline() Aligns each locus with MAFFT and masks poorly aligned columns with DECIPHER::MaskAlignment(). Katoh & Standley (2013); Wright (2024)
run_marker_screening() Screens each locus alignment for coverage, length and substitution saturation, by regressing uncorrected p-distance against the gamma-corrected K80 distance. The slope threshold below which a locus is rejected is a PhyloCactus criterion, not a published saturation test; the references cover the distance model only. Kimura (1980); Jin & Nei (1990)
clean_taxonomic_names() Keeps the sequences whose name is in the checklist of Cactaceae, ignoring differences in spaces, hyphens and underscores, and renames them to the spelling of the checklist. Korotkova et al. (2021)
run_joint_realignment() Realigns each locus with MAFFT after the ingroup and outgroup sequences are combined. Katoh & Standley (2013)

Supermatrix

Function Description Reference
run_concatenation_pipeline() Concatenates the locus alignments into a supermatrix and writes partition maps in RAxML format (read by RAxML-NG, ModelTest-NG and IQ-TREE) and NEXUS format, with configuration files for PartitionFinder2 and MrBayes. Not applicable

Model Selection and Maximum-Likelihood Inference

Function Description Reference
preprocess_partitions() Checks the supermatrix and partition map with RAxML-NG before model selection. Kozlov et al. (2019)
run_modeltest_ng() Selects a substitution model for each partition with ModelTest-NG under the AICc. Darriba et al. (2020)
build_constraint_scaffold() Builds a multifurcating constraint tree that enforces the monophyly of subfamilies and major clades of Cactaceae established in published phylogenies. Guerrero et al. (2019)
calculate_ml_tree() Estimates the maximum-likelihood tree with RAxML-NG under the partition models and the constraint tree, from 25 random and 25 parsimony starting trees by default. Kozlov et al. (2019)
map_branch_supports() Maps Felsenstein bootstrap proportions (FBP) or transfer bootstrap expectation (TBE) from the bootstrap replicates onto the maximum-likelihood tree. Felsenstein (1985); Lemoine et al. (2018)

Divergence Time Estimation

Function Description Reference
rescale_tree() Multiplies all branch lengths by a constant before dating with treePL. The factor changes the scale of the rate parameters and the numerical conditioning of the optimization; it does not change which branches treePL treats as too short. Smith & O’Meara (2012)
run_treePL_direct() Runs the treePL binary on a configuration file, after checking that the tree is rooted. Smith & O’Meara (2012)
run_treePL_cv() Selects the rate-smoothing parameter by cross-validation, classifies the shape of the cross-validation curve, and dates the tree. Sanderson (2002); Maurin (2020)
automate_treePL() Selects the optimization parameters and the smoothing value by cross-validation on the maximum-likelihood tree, dates it, and applies them to every temporal bootstrap replicate. Smith & O’Meara (2012); Maurin (2020)
send_run_notification() Sends an email when a long analysis ends, reporting status, timings and output paths. A failure to send does not stop the analysis. blastula R package, https://github.com/rstudio/blastula

Comparison, Figures and IUCN Data

Function Description Reference
validate_phylogenies() Compares the focal tree with published trees using the Robinson-Foulds and Different Phylogenetic Information distances, and projects the distances into tree space by multidimensional scaling. Robinson & Foulds (1981); Smith (2020)
integrate_publication_tree() Maps support values onto the chronogram and the maximum-likelihood tree and collapses nodes with FBP below 0.70 into polytomies for the publication figures. Hillis & Bull (1993)
get_iucn_data() Retrieves the IUCN Red List assessment of a species through rredlist: category, criteria, population trend, countries of occurrence, endemism, habitats and threats. IUCN (2026)
scale_fill_iucn() ggplot2 fill scale with the standard IUCN Red List category colors. IUCN (2026)

Molecular Identification: the Library (Tutorial 5, Steps 1 to 4)

Function Description Reference
assemble_barcoding_dataset() Names the clusters of the phylotaR mining of the phylogeny by locus, cuts records over 2000 bases to the extent of the shorter records of their locus, reconciles every name against the checklist and, optionally, adds the user’s own sequences. Bennett et al. (2018); Korotkova et al. (2021)
curate_barcoding_markers() Aligns each locus with MAFFT, puts every sequence on one strand and masks poorly aligned columns, with the parameters of the phylogeny’s ingroup. Katoh & Standley (2013); Wright (2024)
screen_barcoding_markers() Decides which loci enter the library by the number of species with two or more sequences, and flags saturation and possible paralogy without excluding.
finalize_barcoding_library() Excludes and declares non-homologous sequences, collapses identical sequences of one species and writes the library, one alignment per locus.
extract_barcoding_plastome_loci() Crops the library loci from GenBank plastomes as extra records; a plastome does not add a locus that a library record of the same specimen already holds.
barcoding_outgroup_taxids() The NCBI Taxonomy IDs of the six genera of Anacampserotaceae, Portulacaceae and Talinaceae that the outgroup control asks the library about.

Molecular Identification: Validation (Tutorial 5, Steps 5 to 10)

Function Description Reference
build_barcoding_folds() Builds the validation folds: scheme E leaves one sequence out and asks for its species, scheme G leaves a whole species out and asks for its genus.
analyze_barcode_gap() Intraspecific distances and the distance to the nearest neighbour of another species, per locus, uncorrected and K80, with a candidate threshold reported, never imposed. Meyer & Paulay (2005); Kimura (1980)
classify_barcoding_folds() Classifies the folds by nearest neighbour (each query added to the training alignment with MAFFT --add) or by IdTaxa, in three states, in parallel processes of one machine. Katoh & Frith (2012); Murali et al. (2018)
generate_barcoding_job_scripts() Writes the SLURM job array and the R script that classify the folds in chunks on a computing cluster.
merge_barcoding_chunks() Merges the chunks of a cluster run into the tables one process would write, and checks that every query appears once.
run_barcoding_controls() Negative controls: label permutation for leakage ("CN1"), outgroup queries from the sister lineages ("CN2") and resubstitution bias ("CN3").
sweep_barcoding_threshold() Sweeps the threshold of remoteness of the nearest neighbour, or the confidence of IdTaxa, and writes the species threshold of each locus used by the identification.
summarise_barcoding_metrics() Per locus and scheme: species correct, genus correct, wrong species, wrong genus and unassigned, and precision and recall per class.
summarise_barcoding_genus_discrimination() How well each locus tells apart the species of each genus in the folds, shown in the identification report beside the answer.

Molecular Identification: Identifying a Sample (Tutorial 5, Step 11)

Function Description Reference
identify_barcoding_query() Identifies sequences (FASTA, GenBank flat file or character vector) against the library, locus by locus, with IdTaxa, in three states, and writes the report. Murali et al. (2018)
identify_barcoding_samples() Identifies every sample of a sample sheet through the route its input type requires.
identify_barcoding_assembly() Maps the library loci onto an assembly with minimap2, extracts them with samtools and identifies them. Li (2018); Danecek et al. (2021)
identify_barcoding_reads() Assembles the plastome and the nuclear ribosomal DNA from paired Illumina reads with fastp and GetOrganelle, then identifies them. Chen et al. (2018); Jin et al. (2020)
report_barcoding_identification() Writes the self-contained HTML report of a run: answer per locus, agreement between loci, alternatives, sampling of the genus and provenance.
plot_barcoding_identification() Draws the answer per locus of an identification, and the sampling of the named genera, from the tables of its report.
plot_barcoding_identification_summary() Draws the answers of several identifications side by side, one row per identification and one column per locus.

Help Pages 

library(PhyloCactus)

?run_alignment_pipeline
?calculate_ml_tree
?automate_treePL

The functions used for checks within the tutorials, such as check_calibration_consistency(), report_bound_adherence(), classify_constrained_nodes(), audit_calibration_support() and report_smoothing_sensitivity(), are documented in their manual pages and in the tutorials where they are used.
